title: Cohomology of an ordered localization model is element-power torsion
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, and use its module-sheaf category on the one-object bottom site with a chosen derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $I$ be a finitely generated ideal of $A$, let $T$ be a cochain complex with augmentation $\epsilon_T:T\to A[0]$, and assume the ordered localization-model predicate for $(I,T,\epsilon_T)$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-complex-cech-data]. For every $s\in I$, every integer $i$, and every element $x$ of the value of $H^i(T)$ at the unique site object, there exists $k\in\mathbb N$ with $s^k x=0$. No coefficient module or derived Hom conclusion is part of this assertion.

source.place: Tag 0A6R, lemma-local-cohomology-adjoint; cohomology of an ordered localization model is element-power torsion

proof.text: First prove the unit-ideal Godement complex is zero in the derived category. Apply its proved ordered-model theorem to the singleton generating list (1). In its witness C, the only possible nonzero terms are degrees zero and one: in higher degrees an increasing tuple into Fin 1 cannot exist. The first differential is an isomorphism, because the unique singleton coordinate identifies it with A to A[1/1], an isomorphism by IsLocalization.atUnit. The two-term complex is acyclic by the mono and epi exactness criteria. Cohomology on the derived category transports this acyclicity to the Godement object.

proof.text: Choose a finite generating list f of I and its ordered model C from hT. Put B=A[1/s]. Since s lies in I and its image is a unit, the extended ideal is the unit ideal; hence the image list generates the unit ideal. Apply the Godement ordered-model theorem over B to that image list, obtaining D. The proved ordered scalar isomorphism identifies the termwise scalar extension of C with D. Its derived comparison to the unit-ideal Godement complex and the preceding step show D is acyclic. No change-of-generators contraction is needed.

source.place: Tags 0A6R and 0ALZ, lemma-local-cohomology-adjoint and lemma-torsion-change-rings; with algebraization.tex Tag 099D(d), lemma-all-rings

proof.text: Construct explicitly the equivalence between the one-object bottom-site module sheaves and ordinary modules, using evaluation and constant modules. Evaluation is therefore exact. The scalar-extension section isomorphisms commute with every differential, by their normalization on 1 tensor x and the proved scalar-extension map formula. They give a cochain isomorphism from evaluated C tensored with B to evaluated D, which is acyclic. Flatness of localization makes extension of scalars exact, so its homology comparison shows that localization of each H^i(C) is zero. The given derived model isomorphism induces an isomorphism H^i(C) to H^i(T), so localization of each H^i(T) is zero too.

source.place: Tags 0A6R and 0ALZ, lemma-local-cohomology-adjoint and lemma-torsion-change-rings; with algebraization.tex Tag 099D(d), lemma-all-rings

proof.text: For each x in the evaluated H^i(T), its image 1 tensor x in its zero localized module vanishes. Apply IsLocalization.tensorProduct_isLocalizedModule and IsLocalizedModule.eq_zero_iff. The resulting annihilator belongs to the submonoid of powers of s, so write it as s^k and obtain s^k times x equals zero. All constructions allow the zero ring, s=0 or nilpotent, repeated generators, and an empty initial list.

lean.statement:
theorem ringComplex_cech_cohomology_power_torsion
    (A : CommRingCat.{u}) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (RingSiteModules A)]
    (I : {I : Ideal A // I.FG})
    (T : CochainComplex (RingSiteModules A) ℤ) (εT : T ⟶ ringComplexSingle A)
    (hT : RingComplexHasCechModel A I.val T εT)
    (s : A) (hs : s ∈ I.val) :
    ∀ (i : ℤ) (x : (T.homology i).val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩)),
      ∃ k : ℕ, s ^ k • x = 0
